card.name: Verbs right before a time reference
card.fires_on: Short verbs or linking words (was, appeared, made, have, in, last) that come just before a date, a time phrase, or a past-event marker. The subject is often a thing or person whose origin or history is being described.

modes.label: Was/appeared before a date
modes.description: A past-tense verb about when something was built, written, or first arose, where a year or period comes next.
modes.example: The Stadttheater (Municipal Theatre) [bottom left picture)<< was>> built in 19001

modes.label: Comparison to a time
modes.description: A small word before a time word such as last year or placebo group, in a comparison.
modes.example: Population estimates for the 10 most abundant species surveyed were similar to<< last>> year and to the 199

modes.label: Since-clause verb
modes.description: A verb after a subject in a clause about when something began or was first proposed.
modes.example: However, since antimatter<< was>> first envisaged by Nobel Prize-winning scientist

card.writes: It nudges the model toward time words about the future or upcoming, such as upcoming, future, tomorrow, and away from since-type words.
card.plain: It fires on small verbs just before a date or time phrase, where the text is about to say when something happened.
